attractions.name: Mount Yasur, Tanna
attractions.desc: One of the most accessible active volcanoes in the world, its viewing platforms sitting close enough to the crater rim to feel the ground shake and hear the roar of eruptions directly. It has been almost continuously active for at least 800 years, making it a reliable, if unpredictable, natural spectacle. Evening visits offer the most dramatic view, as glowing lava becomes visible against the darkening sky.

attractions.name: Champagne Beach, Espiritu Santo
attractions.desc: A wide crescent of powder-white sand and clear turquoise water often ranked among the best beaches in the South Pacific. Its name comes from the fizzing bubbles that rise through the sand in certain spots at low tide. It remains relatively undeveloped, with just a few small local stalls rather than large resort infrastructure.

attractions.name: The Blue Holes
attractions.desc: Freshwater swimming holes scattered around Espiritu Santo, their vivid turquoise color a result of exceptionally clear, mineral-filtered water. Riverbank rope swings at several of the holes add a playful element to what is otherwise a peaceful swimming spot. They offer a refreshing freshwater contrast to the island's saltwater beaches and diving sites.

attractions.name: Port Vila markets
attractions.desc: A produce and handicraft market that anchors the capital's waterfront, selling fresh tropical fruit, kava, and woven goods from vendors representing Vanuatu's many islands and language groups. The town itself, wrapped around a natural harbour, offers a relaxed introduction to the country before heading to more remote islands. It remains the main transport hub for onward travel throughout the archipelago.

attractions.name: SS President Coolidge wreck diving
attractions.desc: One of the world's largest and most accessible shipwreck dives, a former luxury liner turned troop transport that sank just off Espiritu Santo in 1942 after striking mines. Divers can explore multiple decks, including cargo holds still containing jeeps, guns, and personal effects from World War II. Its accessibility from shore, combined with the wreck's scale, has made it a bucket-list site for wreck diving enthusiasts.

attractions.name: Pentecost Island land diving
attractions.desc: The origin of modern bungee jumping, this traditional ritual involves young men leaping from tall wooden towers with only vines tied to their ankles, performed each year as part of a yam harvest ceremony. It's considered a rite of passage and remains deeply tied to local custom rather than staged purely for visitors. Access requires travel to Pentecost Island specifically during the April to June ceremonial season.

itinerary.label: Days 1–2
itinerary.title: Port Vila
itinerary.desc: Markets, waterfront cafes, and a day trip to nearby Efate beaches.
itinerary.cost: Most market visits and waterfront walks are free; an Efate day tour costs $40–70.
itinerary.food: Try lap lap at a local market stall — Vanuatu's national dish, worth trying in its traditional form.

itinerary.label: Days 3–4
itinerary.title: Tanna
itinerary.desc: A flight to see Mount Yasur's eruptions up close, ideally at dusk.
itinerary.cost: A guided Mount Yasur volcano tour costs about $100–150 per person, including transport and the mandatory guide.
itinerary.food: Meals are typically arranged through your guesthouse, given Tanna's limited independent restaurant scene.

itinerary.label: Days 5–6
itinerary.title: Espiritu Santo
itinerary.desc: Champagne Beach and the Blue Holes to close the trip.
itinerary.logistics: ~1h flight from Tanna via Port Vila
itinerary.cost: Snorkeling or diving the historic SS President Coolidge wreck costs $80–150 depending on the operator.
itinerary.food: A relaxed beach lunch at Champagne Beach is a fitting way to close the trip.

goodToKnow.safety: Very safe; normal caution around active volcano viewing areas
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Small domestic flights are needed to reach the outer islands
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Bauerfield International Airport (VLI) in Port Vila is Vanuatu's main gateway

food.name: Lap lap
food.desc: Vanuatu's national dish: grated root vegetable baked with coconut milk and meat or fish.

food.name: Coconut crab
food.desc: A large land crab considered a local delicacy, though now protected in some areas.

food.name: Tropical fruits
food.desc: Papaya, pineapple, and passionfruit grow abundantly across the islands.

food.name: Kava
food.desc: A ceremonial drink shared widely across Melanesia, with strong roots in Vanuatu culture.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Vanuatu?
faq.a: Not for most Western passport holders (EU, UK, US, Canada) for short stays.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Bauerfield International (VLI) in Port Vila, Vanuatu's main gateway.

faq.q: Is it safe to see Mount Yasur up close?
faq.a: Yes, with a licensed local guide — access is carefully managed and closed when activity levels are deemed unsafe, but on permitted days you can get remarkably close to the active crater.

faq.q: What is the land-diving ritual on Pentecost Island?
faq.a: A traditional ceremony, the origin of modern bungee jumping, held seasonally, typically April to June — visiting requires specific timing and a respectful, guided approach through a local operator.

daysReason: 6 days covers Port Vila, Tanna's volcano, and Espiritu Santo at an island pace. 3–4 works for just Port Vila and Tanna; 8+ lets you slow down or add Pentecost Island's land-diving ritual in season.
visa: Not required for EU, UK, US, and Canadian citizens for short stays — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Monte Yasur, Tanna
attractions.desc: Um dos vulcões ativos mais acessíveis do mundo, com os seus miradouros situados suficientemente perto da borda da cratera para sentir o chão a tremer e ouvir o rugido das erupções diretamente. Está quase continuamente ativo há pelo menos 800 anos, tornando-o um espetáculo natural fiável, embora imprevisível. Visitas ao entardecer oferecem a vista mais dramática, à medida que a lava incandescente se torna visível contra o céu que escurece.

attractions.name: Praia Champagne, Espiritu Santo
attractions.desc: Uma larga faixa de areia branca em pó e água turquesa clara, muitas vezes classificada entre as melhores praias do Pacífico Sul. O seu nome vem das bolhas efervescentes que sobem pela areia em certos pontos na maré baixa. Continua relativamente pouco desenvolvida, com apenas algumas pequenas bancas locais em vez de grande infraestrutura de resort.

attractions.name: Os Buracos Azuis
attractions.desc: Piscinas de água doce espalhadas por Espiritu Santo, com a sua cor turquesa vívida resultante de água excecionalmente clara e filtrada por minerais. Baloiços de corda na margem em vários dos buracos acrescentam um elemento lúdico ao que é de outra forma um tranquilo local de natação. Oferecem um contraste refrescante de água doce face às praias de água salgada e locais de mergulho da ilha.

attractions.name: Mercados de Port Vila
attractions.desc: Um mercado de produtos e artesanato que ancora a frente marítima da capital, vendendo fruta tropical fresca, kava, e produtos tecidos de vendedores representando os muitos grupos de ilhas e línguas de Vanuatu. A própria vila, envolta à volta de um porto natural, oferece uma introdução relaxada ao país antes de seguir para ilhas mais remotas. Continua a ser o principal centro de transporte para viagens posteriores por todo o arquipélago.

attractions.name: Mergulho no destroço do SS President Coolidge
attractions.desc: Um dos maiores e mais acessíveis mergulhos de destroços do mundo, um antigo transatlântico de luxo transformado em transporte de tropas que afundou mesmo ao largo de Espiritu Santo em 1942 depois de atingir minas. Os mergulhadores podem explorar vários conveses, incluindo porões de carga ainda contendo jipes, armas, e pertences pessoais da Segunda Guerra Mundial. A sua acessibilidade a partir da costa, combinada com a escala do destroço, tornou-o um mergulho de lista de desejos para entusiastas de mergulho em destroços.

attractions.name: Salto de terra em Pentecost
attractions.desc: A origem do bungee jumping moderno, este ritual tradicional envolve jovens saltando de altas torres de madeira com apenas videiras amarradas aos tornozelos, realizado todos os anos como parte de uma cerimónia de colheita de inhame. É considerado um rito de passagem e continua profundamente ligado ao costume local em vez de encenado puramente para visitantes. O acesso requer viagem à Ilha Pentecost especificamente durante a época cerimonial de abril a junho.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–2
itinerary.title: Port Vila
itinerary.desc: Mercados, cafés à beira-mar, e uma excursão de um dia às praias próximas de Efate.

itinerary.label: Dias 3–4
itinerary.title: Tanna
itinerary.desc: Um voo para ver as erupções do Monte Yasur de perto, idealmente ao entardecer.

itinerary.label: Dias 5–6
itinerary.title: Espiritu Santo
itinerary.desc: A Praia Champagne e os Buracos Azuis para fechar a viagem.
itinerary.logistics: ~1h de voo desde Tanna via Port Vila

goodToKnow.safety: Muito seguro; cuidado normal à volta de áreas de observação de vulcão ativo
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Pequenos voos domésticos são necessários para chegar às ilhas exteriores
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Bauerfield International Airport (VLI) in Port Vila is Vanuatu's main gateway

food.name: Lap lap
food.desc: O prato nacional de Vanuatu: raiz ralada assada com leite de coco e carne ou peixe.

food.name: Caranguejo de coco
food.desc: Um grande caranguejo terrestre considerado uma iguaria local, embora agora protegido em algumas áreas.

food.name: Frutas tropicais
food.desc: Papaia, ananás, e maracujá crescem em abundância pelas ilhas.

food.name: Kava
food.desc: Uma bebida cerimonial partilhada amplamente pela Melanésia, com raízes fortes na cultura de Vanuatu.
